cur:catacombs-jonah-sarcophagus-vatican.summary: The front is dominated by a lively seascape telling the story of Jonah – thrown overboard, swallowed and cast up by the sea-monster, and resting under his vine. Around it are smaller scenes including Christ raising Lazarus from his tomb and Moses striking the rock. Jonah's three days in the monster were read by Christ himself as a sign of his resurrection, here paired with the raising of Lazarus.
facts: Commons dates the front to about 280–300 and records its provenance as the Vatican necropolis.
Its date makes it one of the earliest sarcophagi with explicit Christian narrative, made before the Peace of the Church (313).
cur:catacombs-jonah-sarcophagus-vatican.notes: Christ appears in the small raising of Lazarus at the upper left; the Jonah cycle forms most of the relief.

Q116256893.summary: Lightly engraved into the centre of a green glass dish, Christ stands holding a staff toward the wrapped, mummy-like figure of Lazarus in his tomb, with another figure beside them, all within a wreath of leafy ornament and a ribbed rim. On a vessel perhaps used at table, the raising of Lazarus proclaimed Christ's power over death, one of the most popular subjects in early Christian art.
facts: The dish is about 24 cm in diameter and was given to the Met by J. Pierpont Morgan in 1917.
In Late Antique art Christ is often shown raising Lazarus with a staff or wand, touching the tomb in which Lazarus stands bound in grave-cloths.
Q116256893.notes: The image shows a crack running across the dish; the engraving is faint and the third figure is not securely identified.
